title: Mara and the Border
premise: Paloma Pemberton, a freelance interpreter who handles the delegations and disappearances governments prefer unattributed, is summoned when Flight 447's passenger manifest evaporates from every database while the plane is still airborne. Aboard is Ilan Voss, a defector carrying proof that the peace process she has spent two years interpreting was engineered to fail — and someone wants both him and the evidence to never land. Paloma must smuggle Voss across a militarized border using her linguistic access and a network of old debts, unsure whether he is a genuine defector or bait designed to expose her. In the end she chooses love over duty: she burns her own cover identity to get Voss out, exposing the sabotage at the cost of everything she was.
about_author: Odile Thackeray is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass booths in Geneva, Vienna, and places without names. She writes thrillers about people whose job is to be trusted by everyone and known by no one.

chapters.title: The Glass Booth
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. During a fractious ceasefire negotiation in Vienna, Paloma interprets a threat she deliberately softens — and watches it detonate anyway. The delegation collapses, and her handler, Merrick, tells her there's one more job before she goes home. Emotional beat: the quiet erosion of believing words can hold anything together.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Flight 447 is forty minutes from landing when every record of it vanishes — booking systems, radar archives, even her own email confirmation. Merrick shows her the only surviving artifact: a photo of Ilan Voss boarding, holding a case chained to his wrist. Emotional beat: vertigo; reality itself edited while she watched.

chapters.title: What Voss Carried
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, recovered later as testimony. He describes the flight, the case of documents proving the peace framework was sabotaged from inside, and the moment the cabin crew stopped answering questions. He lands at an airstrip that officially does not exist. Emotional beat: cold clarity of a man who planned his betrayal for years.

chapters.title: Debts and Dialects
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. To reach the border zone she calls in favors from three people who owe her silence: a customs officer, a smuggler-priest, and a woman she once betrayed. Each extraction costs her something irreplaceable. Emotional beat: the arithmetic of loyalty, paid in installments.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Plane
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She finds Voss hiding in a decommissioned chapel near the border, paranoid and half-starved. Their first conversation happens in four languages, testing each other's truths. He warns her he may be bait — and so may she. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people built entirely of aliases.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Winter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The crossing goes wrong at a checkpoint where the guard speaks a dialect only Paloma knows — and recognizes her voice from intercepted recordings. She talks them through, but Merrick's team is now tracking her signal. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into performance; her gift becomes her exposure.

chapters.title: The Bait Confesses
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Cornered in a safehouse, Voss admits the sabotage documents are real but incomplete — the final page naming the architect is with a contact inside the delegation Paloma once served. He also admits he chose her name deliberately. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with tenderness; he needed someone who could not refuse.

chapters.title: Everything Attributed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She infiltrates the delegation's closing summit under a borrowed credential and retrieves the final page, discovering the saboteur is Merrick himself, selling failure to both sides. Alarms rise as she walks out with the truth in her coat lining. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Border Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma and Voss's alternating POV. The climax: a night crossing through a river gorge as Merrick's operatives close in. Paloma broadcasts the sabotage documents over open frequencies in six languages, making herself the story too loud to erase. Voss takes a bullet shielding her; they make the far bank. Emotional beat: love chosen openly, at last, against every duty.

chapters.title: Interpreter, Unemployed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, months later. The scandal has ended the peace process and begun honest ones; Voss recovers under a new name, hers among them. She declines every offer to come back inside, opening a small translation office in a port town where nobody asks questions. Emotional beat: belonging finally found not in a country or a cause, but in a person and a plain, unclassified life.
